title: Assert real toggle/selection state (not just tapped-label presence) in progress_p0_test.dart and scheduler_p0_test.dart chip/segment tests
rule: TQ-7/TQ-8 (assertion weaker than the failure mode under test)

evidence.quote: // The chip label is still visible (toggle rendered without crash).
// Toggle label still visible (no crash, state updated).
// After selecting Dafim, the pace input label should reference "Dafim".

why: Each cited test taps a chip/segment whose label was already visible before the tap (e.g. 'Last 30 Days', 'Track learning only', 'Dafim' are all rendered pre-tap as available options), then re-asserts the SAME label is present post-tap. RecentActivityScreen's chip is a real FilterChip with a `selected` bool the test never reads. A regression that wires onSelected to a no-op — tap does nothing — would leave identical text on screen and pass all 4 tests; one test's own comment even claims 'state updated' while checking only visibility, not state.
recommendation: Assert the actual post-tap state, e.g. `tester.widget<FilterChip>(find.widgetWithText(FilterChip, 'Last 30 Days')).selected == true`, or another concrete tap-dependent effect (chart data range, provider value), instead of re-checking the tapped label's mere presence.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 4 tests asserts a concrete, tap-dependent state change (selected flag, updated derived value, or provider read) rather than only the continued presence of the tapped label.

corrections: 'sites: 4' overcounts: recent_activity_screen.dart:777 is supporting proof, not a 4th weakened-assertion test site (only 3 exist: progress_p0_test.dart:399,591; scheduler_p0_test.dart:441) — should be sites:3. Also 'Track learning only' (lifetime_knowledge_screen.dart) and 'Dafim' (goal_setup_screen.dart) are SegmentedButton, not FilterChip as the 'why' text implies applies to 'RecentActivityScreen's chip' — only the 'Last 30 Days' site is actually a FilterChip. The tautology argument still holds for SegmentedButton (both segments always render regardless of selection), so the underlying defect is real, just the widget-type generalization is imprecise.
